Title: Coronavirus: 65-year-old Indian man died in Agra after hospitals refused to admit him without a COVID-19 test
# Coronavirus: 65-year-old Indian man died in Agra after hospitals refused to admit him without a COVID-19 test. Coronavirus: Tweeps complain of hospitals refusing to admit critical patients. 65-year-old man passed away after hospitals refused to admit him. India's Armed Forces salute COVID-19 warriors. In a “heartbreaking” incident, a 65-year-old Indian man died in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, after hospitals refused to admit him without a coronavirus test, while he was in a critical condition. Indian news website NDTV shared a video report on May 6, about how RV Pundhir’s family ran from hospital to hospital begging for help but received none. Pundhir a manager at a tractor company, used to visit a private hospital in the city regularly. In April, he needed to go in for dialysis, but the hospital denied entry without a COVID-19 test. The family made many calls for help but got no response from any hospital. They took him from hospital to hospital, only to be turned away. Indian journalist Barkha Dutt has also earlier reported about the Pundhir family's tragedy. She wrote: “A 65-year-old man denied dialysis unless he tests for Corona. He falls sick, can't get an ambulance, turned away from 3 hospitals. He tests negative for Corona, results come after his death.”. Apparently, a viral video shows how the Sarojini Nagar hospital, a government approved COVID-19 treatment center also turned the serious patient away. Reportedly, Pundhir’s grieving family says he died in the car. Tweep @khanism\_ posted: “This has happened in Odisha too… he was a regular patient of Shanti Hospital In Cuttack, where he used to have dialysis but still hospital didn't do his dialysis. He was not allowed to go to the hospital till his tests for Corona were done. Many people are taking to Twitter to question why some hospitals seem to be showing medical negligence, and tagged lawmakers to take legal action in such cases. @ExtrovertNikhil posted: “The federal governments should not hesitate to invoke stringent provisions including registration of FIRs, cancellation of licenses and even state takeover of private hospitals if they refuse to take in patients or give them ER procedures for critically ill or institutional care.”.

# Corona patient dies after family unplugs ventilator to turn on cooler. ## In a shocking incident, a COVID-19 patient in Rajasthan’s Kota district died after his family disconnected the ventilator to plug in the air cooler to combat the scorching heat. #### IANS. In a shocking incident, a COVID-19 patient in Rajasthan's Kota district died after his family disconnected the ventilator to plug in the air cooler to combat the scorching heat. The incident happened on June 15 in the Maharao Bhimsingh Hospital (MBS) hospital. A committee was formed soon after the death was reported, which will submit its report on Friday at 4 p.m., hospital Medical Superintendent Naveen Saxena told IANS. He said, "We have set up the committee to investigate the incident based on the primary information. The committee includes deputy superintendent of the hospital, nursing superintendent and CMO. We will look into the matter and then shall explore further action for a need to go to the police.". The family members of the COVID-19 patient, who came to meet him in the MBS hospital unplugged the ventilator and had put on the cooler switch which they had brought from outside. The ventilator worked for some time on the battery but later it collapsed and the patient turned critical. The doctors were reported of the patient's critical condition who came rushing and did all they could do to save his life, but the result was unfavourable and the patient died. The doctors were reported of the patient's critical condition who came rushing and did all they could do to save his life, but the result was unfavourable and the patient died. The relatives, on the other hand, attacked the resident doctors after the patient died. Home India Family fined over lavish wedding, groom and 15 others get Corona. # Family fined over lavish wedding, groom and 15 others get Corona. **Jaipur–** The Bhilwara district administration has slapped Rs 6.26 lakh fine on a family for organising a lavish wedding, attended by 250 guests flouting all Covid-19 norms and restrictions, on June 13. While the number of guests was much above the permitted 50, one person died and 15 attendees, including the groom, had tested coronavirus positive by June 27. Officials said the groom’s grand-father died from Covid-19, and his aunt and uncle also tested coronavirus positive. However, the bride and 17 others tested negative. All the 15 Covid-19 patients have been admitted to hospital and over 100 quarantined. The state government slapped a notice on the groom’s father ordering him to foot the bill of the quarantine facility and treatment of infected people by paying Rs 6,26,600 fine. Bhilwara District Magistrate Rajendra Bhatt has asked the Tehsildar to recover the fine from the groom’s father within 3 days, and deposit that in the Chief Minister Relief Fund. Other expenses, to be incurred in coming days, should also be recovered from the groom’s family, the order, issued under the Epidemic Act, added. The order also said the groom, Rizul, and his father Gheesu Lal Rathi didn’t follow the social distancing norms, were not wearing masks and there was no use of sanitiser at the event. #### RELATED ARTICLESMORE FROM AUTHOR. ### Delhi Police File Case Against SFJ Leader Pannun Over Republic Day Threats. ### India Leads in Female STEM Education, but Workforce Participation Still Lags, Report Finds. ### India, Canada Look to Expand Economic Ties, Says Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal. ### Engineers India Completes Record-Breaking 4-Kilometre Pipeline Crossing Under Brahmaputra River. ### ED Raids Builder’s Premises in Haryana in $72 Million Homebuyer Fraud Case. ### Indian Passport Climbs Five Places in Henley Passport Index. ### LEAVE A REPLY Cancel reply. ## Upcoming Events. ### IAGB Republic Day Celebration. ### INDIA New England Spring Wedding Expo. ### INDIA New England 2026 Woman of the Year Gala. ### AIF New England Appreciation Gala 2026.

Officials also said that such reports should be made at least three days before the trip. Arrangement has been made to show the report related to Corona before getting the travel permit (boarding pass). The requirement to show proof of a negative corona before traveling applies to all U.S. or non-U.S. citizens, officials said. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said the measure would be implemented on January 26. “All passengers aged two and over must provide proof that they have not been infected with the coronavirus or have been infected with the coronavirus before entering the United States,” the State Department said in a statement. He clarified that boarding pass can be arranged for those who are unable to submit such proof. “If you are planning an international flight, you must submit proof of a negative corona three days in advance,” the statement said.
